The agent stops later (around Turn 16) once it realizes the previous data points were insufficient or ambiguous, but the primary issue was misinterpreting a fact, not failing to recognize completion. Additionally, the error spans Turn 1 (no prior result), so claiming errors start at Turn 1 due to 'unaware stopping' is logically inconsistent. The agent needed better fact-checking (hallucination recovery) and a task-completion check after Turn 6, not just a stop check at the end.
